rule.description: A function matches when its body holds three or more separate nested scopes (blocks at depth >= 2), each carrying at least 12 direct work units (direct statements plus direct let bindings). Multiple helper-sized scopes trapped in one function body is the structural signature of a call graph collapsed three or more levels deep into a single monolithic method.

checks.description: DEEPLY_INLINED_METHOD via Dylint structural measurement: every function of the target crate is walked and each nested block records its direct statements and let bindings; a function is a match when at least MIN_DENSE_SCOPES=3 blocks at depth >= MIN_BLOCK_DEPTH=2 each hold at least MIN_BLOCK_UNITS=12 direct work units.
checks.detected_relation: owner function -> three or more formerly helper-sized work clusters inlined as sibling or nested scopes of one method body, collapsing the owner-to-helper call levels into a single body
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: deeply_inlined_method names a method whose sub-method implementations were copied into itself; the multi-scope mass measurement detects exactly that collapse without depending on any single naming, text, or diff artifact, and it accepts any repair that decomposes the clusters back into well-scoped functions or otherwise removes the dense scopes.

matches.evidence: dispatch_ip contains 5 dense nested scopes: the two copied link-layer address-resolution clusters (broadcast/multicast mapping, neighbor-cache lookup with ARP request synthesis and with NDISC neighbor-solicitation synthesis) for the IEEE 802.15.4 site and again for the Ethernet site, plus the pre-existing IPv4 fragmentation scope; the resolution clusters each re-create the body of the retained lookup_hardware_addr helper inside the dispatch path.

process_sixlowpan contains 4 dense nested scopes: the FRAG1 reassembly guard cluster (per-fragment validation, assembler slot management) with the sixlowpan_to_ipv6 decompression core copied inside the assembler callback, and the IPHC decompression core (IPv6 header re-materialization, NHC extension-header and UDP decompression) copied into the direct-reception arm.

dispatch_sixlowpan contains 3 dense nested scopes: the compressed-size accounting cluster formerly held by the sizing helper, the uncompressed-IPv6-to-6LoWPAN compression core copied into the transmit callback for the non-fragmented path, and the fragmentation emission plan reworked as a nested plan block.

Socket::process contains 4 dense nested scopes: the two halves of ACK interpretation (lease-parameter validation, then configuration assembly and the RFC 2131 renew/rebind timeline derivation) are each copied into the Requesting arm and again into the Renewing arm, replacing the removed parse_ack helper once per state.

excluded: Functions holding only one dense nested scope are outside the rule: src/socket/tcp.rs Socket::process and src/socket/dns.rs Socket::process carry large but single-cluster bodies in the pinned baseline and never reach the multiplicity threshold; a single inlined branch does not constitute the deeply inlined method relation.

The pre-existing IPv4 fragmentation scope in src/iface/interface/mod.rs dispatch_ip is measured like all other scopes, but it is part of the upstream implementation and occurs once per function, so it alone does not make the function a match.

Functions in ephemeral cfg-off modules and closures are separate measurements with their own identities: closure bodies are measured as their own functions, so a copied cluster placed inside a closure cannot inflate the enclosing function's scope count.
